scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC4 and PC5 (Location A VLAN 10, 172.16.10.0/24) opened ticket #7041: they can no
longer reach their gateway (172.16.10.1) or anything off their VLAN. Laptop0 on
VLAN 20 in the same Location is unaffected. The team has been staring at router0
and is convinced its VLAN-10 sub-interface failed during the last change --
"router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface (eth0.10) went down and stopped serving VLAN 10."
Please confirm the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault and identify the down
interface.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath3-mswitch1-vlan10-trunk-misconfig: mswitch1's
VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) toward router0 is administratively down. With
eth0.10 down on mswitch1, no VLAN 10 frames cross the uplink, so PC4/PC5 cannot ARP
or reach their gateway (172.16.10.1). VLAN 20 rides eth0.20, which is up -- exactly
why Laptop0 is unaffected.

The TWIST: the ticket blames router0's VLAN-10 sub-interface. router0 is HEALTHY --
its eth0.10 (172.16.10.1) is up and configured; the gateway itself never failed.
This is first-hop / symptom-site bias aimed at the L3 device: the team assumes the
gateway must be down because the gateway is unreachable. A decisive tell: the break
is VLAN-scoped (VLAN 10 dead, VLAN 20 fine) and lives on the L2 trunk between the
hosts and router0. If router0's eth0.10 were the problem you would still see VLAN 10
frames reach router0 (and fail there); instead the frames never leave mswitch1
because its eth0.10 trunk subif is down.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = mswitch1 (eth0.10 trunk subif
down). The agent must localise from evidence -- mswitch1's down eth0.10 versus
router0's healthy eth0.10 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on router0. An agent
that "confirms the router0 VLAN-10 sub-interface fault" has followed the accusation
instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0.10 up` on mswitch1
scoring_axes: must-identify-trunk-subif: VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) on mswitch1 down

agent.diagnosis_text:
Router0’s VLAN-10 sub-interface is healthy and not the cause. On router0, eth0.10 is UP/LOWER_UP with 172.16.10.1/24 configured, but it cannot ARP for hosts (ip neigh shows INCOMPLETE for 172.16.10.4). PC4 on VLAN 10 has a valid IP and default route but shows ARP incomplete for 172.16.10.1, and can only reach PC5 locally. This pattern indicates a Layer-2 break in VLAN 10 between the access switch and the router.

Localization: the uplink trunk between switch1 and the distribution switch mswitch1 is broken for VLAN 10. Evidence on mswitch1 shows eth0.10@eth0 is DOWN, while eth0.20@eth0 is UP. On switch1, eth0.10 is UP and br_vlan10 is UP. On mswitch1, the trunk toward router0 (eth4.10) is UP, so only the segment toward switch1 is down for VLAN 10. Laptop0 on VLAN 20 is unaffected, consistent with VLAN 20 working end-to-end.

Mechanism: with mswitch1 eth0.10 down, VLAN 10 frames from switch1 never reach mswitch1 or router0, so ARP fails on both ends and routing to/off VLAN 10 is lost, while intra-switch VLAN 10 traffic (pc5→pc4) still works.

Root cause: mswitch1’s VLAN 10 sub-interface on the uplink to switch1 (eth0.10) is down, likely left administratively down or misconfigured during the last change.

Corrective fix: on mswitch1, bring up eth0.10 and ensure it is enslaved to br_vlan10 (e.g., ip link set dev eth0.10 up; bridge master br_vlan10 set dev eth0.10), then verify ARP and pings to 172.16.10.1 from PC4/PC5.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-trunk-subif: VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) on mswitch1 down
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies mswitch1's VLAN 10 trunk subinterface (eth0.10) as down and prescribes bringing eth0.10 up on mswitch1.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerate-router0: notes router0's eth0.10 / gateway 172.16.10.1 is up and not the cause
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router0's eth0.10 is UP/LOWER_UP with 172.16.10.1 and declares router0 not the cause, localizing the fault to mswitch1.
The agent recommends bringing up mswitch1's eth0.10 and ensuring it's enslaved to br_vlan10 (ip link set dev eth0.10 up; bridge master br_vlan10 set dev eth0.10), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's observations (router eth0.10 UP, router ARP INCOMPLETE for PC, switch1 eth0.10 UP, mswitch1 eth0.10 DOWN, eth0.20 UP) directly support its inference that VLAN10 is broken on mswitch1 rather than router0; the writeup cites the exact interfaces and a correct remediation.
